entries.name: Booderee National Park

facts.claim: Booderee National Park is Aboriginal land managed jointly by Parks Australia and the Wreck Bay Aboriginal Community; a park pass is required.

A 1-day vehicle (including motorcycle) pass is $20 ($10 concession); multi-day and annual passes are $80 and $110 per the same page. The entry station is currently closed; passes are sold online, at the visitor centre or from a van at the Jervis Bay Supermarket.
The park site lists beaches, Booderee Botanic Gardens, Cape St George lighthouse, walks and half-day and full-day itineraries.
NSW national parks passes are not valid in Booderee and Wreck Bay village is an Aboriginal settlement closed to the public.

entries.hours: Open daily (check Parks Australia for gate and alert notices)
entries.ticketUrl_note: Parks Australia's own park site; page title 'Booderee National Park | Parks Australia' (parksaustralia.gov.au/booderee redirects there).

entries.cost_note: $20 per vehicle, 1-day pass (booderee.gov.au passes page); concession $10; NSW passes not valid.

entries.name: Hyams Beach

Wikivoyage still reports a Guinness-record claim for Hyams Beach; Guinness has no whitest-sand category (travel press).
Hyams Beach lies beside Booderee National Park, which has its own pass.

entries.name: Pigeon House Mountain

facts.claim: Pigeon House Mountain Didthul walking track near Ulladulla, in the southern section of Morton National Park, is steep with ladders near the summit; best walked in dry weather; the NPWS page lists 7.1 km return, Grade 4 (a search summary of the same page reported 5 km return, 2.5-3.5 h; the figure conflicts).
Hours 7am to 7pm daily on the NPWS page. Park entry fees apply only at Fitzroy Falls ($4/vehicle) and the Bundanoon area ($8/vehicle), so none at Pigeon House.
Views over the Budawang Wilderness cliffs and gorges, on clear days as far as Jervis Bay and Bermagui.

entries.name: Narooma

facts.claim: Narooma is a pleasant coastal town in Eurobodalla with beautiful beaches and a salt-water inlet, population about 8,500.
Day trips and dives to Montague Island, 9 km offshore, leave from Narooma; scuba dives with Narooma Charters ($80 single dive, 2017).

facts.claim: Ulladulla is largely a service town for agriculture, fishing and tourism with 'few attractions likely to be of interest' by themselves, but it has pleasant beaches and is a convenient base; Ulladulla and Mollymook together are a popular holiday destination.

entries.name: Jervis Bay

facts.claim: Jervis Bay is a large protected bay 120 km south of Sydney, famous for white-sand beaches, safe swimming and snorkelling; humpback whales and dolphins are regular visitors and there is a fairy penguin colony.
Jervis Bay Marine Park covers 100 km of coast; Jervis Bay Village and Murrays Beach are in the Commonwealth Jervis Bay Territory, which charges separate park entry.
